summary: The no-export GPU cube check is implemented in code and matches the user-revised scope. cube_check.inspect_cube requires an open, prepared cube. It checks that seen timestamps equal delivered ones, drains the cube and checks that no owners are pending. It then checks the device of both bank arrays and the uint64 (100,) counts layout. Only the 100 counts are copied to the host, and they are compared with ordinal%99 counts. That rule matches mpi_cube ACTIVE_BINS=99, so bin 99 must stay all zero. array_checks enforces the exact (100,32,512,1024) float32 shape, the byte count and C-contiguous layout. It walks every pixel in 1M-element views (1 MiB bool predicates) and returns only scalar .item() flags. The finite check runs on every chunk, and the result must satisfy nonzero == (count>0). The cube path has no sums .get(), no host cube allocation, no MPI merge, no reference call and no file writes. runner.py calls inspect_cube only on ECC BD ranks, after the loop and the drain gates and outside the timer. It then calls task.sample('cube_verified'), which enforces at least 4 GiB of free device memory. audit.audit_cube independently recomputes per-BD counts and requires exact per-bin records and the no-copy/no-export flags. The global disjoint-union check makes per-BD counts add up to the global counts. campaign.py no longer runs the reference probe or any export. The budget adds up to 4200 s with 11 cases, and the sbatch command matches the allocation that campaign.py checks for. prepare.py copies only committed bytes, pins commit and file/external hashes, and sets files to 0444 and directories to 0555. Vendor stages.py, mpi_cube.py and stage3a cube.py hashes in the supplied receipt match the historical bootstrap01 prepared-bundle.json, so the accumulation algorithms are unchanged. The supplied host receipt reports 107 passed and 64 subtests passed at this HEAD. Two non-blocking findings concern diagnosability and test coverage. There is no GPU/Slurm runtime evidence for this revision, so CUDA behavior, timing and the 300 s ECC stop budget remain unproven. Removing the export does not diagnose the job61373306 stall.

findings.evidence: Progress markers are written only at setup_complete (line 141) and conditioning_complete (line 158). Job61373306 stalled after the loop with an unknown blocked operation, and its progress JSON could not localize the stall. This revision cuts the ECC stop budget from 600 s to 300 s (plan.py:11) without a measured loop time. If the stall recurs, the receipts again cannot tell the event loop, the post-loop gates, inspect_cube and gather/close_shared_memory apart.
findings.requested_change: Before submitting, add small per-rank progress writes after the event loop, after the post-loop gates, after inspect_cube, after comm.gather and after close_shared_memory, with monotonic timestamps. Or record why 300 s is enough given the unknown prior stall.

findings.evidence: The fake-device test monkeypatches array_checks, and array_checks itself is tested only with numpy. No test shows that the production array_checks path touches only scalar reductions on a device-like object, or that the chunk size stays bounded. inspect_cube is also not tested for rejecting a non-open phase, a missing bank, an unknown timestamp, duplicate delivered timestamps or a wrong counts dtype.
findings.requested_change: Add a fake-cp test for array_checks in which slicing records sizes of at most CHECK_ELEMENTS and any non-scalar .get or asnumpy fails. Add the missing inspect_cube rejection cases.
